units.text: She quickly lifts up the shawl, which is hanging down.
ANYA is standing behind it; she bows and runs to her mother, hugs her and runs back to the drawing-room amid general applause.
VARYA stands behind it and bows.
Throws the shawl at PISCHIN, curtseys and runs into the drawing-room.
Leonid hasn’t come yet. I don’t understand what he’s doing so long in town! Everything must be over by now. The estate must be sold; or, if the sale never came off, then why does he stay so long?
units.name: LUBOV

units.text: Uncle has bought it. I’m certain of it.
units.name: VARYA

units.text: Grandmother sent him her authority for him to buy it in her name and transfer the debt to her. She’s doing it for Anya. And I’m certain that God will help us and uncle will buy it.
units.name: VARYA

units.text: Grandmother sent fifteen thousand roubles from Yaroslav to buy the property in her name--she won’t trust us--and that wasn’t even enough to pay the interest.
units.name: LUBOV

units.text: Covers her face with her hands.
My fate will be settled to-day, my fate....
units.name: LUBOV

units.text: Eternal student! He’s already been expelled twice from the university.
units.name: VARYA

units.text: Why are you getting angry, Varya? He’s teasing you about Lopakhin, well what of it? You can marry Lopakhin if you want to, he’s a good, interesting man.... You needn’t if you don’t want to; nobody wants to force you against your will, my darling.
units.name: LUBOV

units.text: I do look at the matter seriously, little mother, to be quite frank. He’s a good man, and I like him.
units.name: VARYA

units.text: Then marry him. I don’t understand what you’re waiting for.
units.name: LUBOV

units.text: I can’t propose to him myself, little mother. People have been talking about him to me for two years now, but he either says nothing, or jokes about it. I understand. He’s getting rich, he’s busy, he can’t bother about me. If I had some money, even a little, even only a hundred roubles, I’d throw up everything and go away. I’d go into a convent.
units.name: VARYA

units.text: A student ought to have sense!
units.name: VARYA

units.text: How ugly you are now, Peter, how old you’ve grown!
units.name: VARYA

units.text: To LUBOV ANDREYEVNA, no longer crying.
But I can’t go on without working, little mother. I want to be doing something every minute.
units.name: VARYA

units.text: Why is Epikhodov here? Who said he could play billiards? I don’t understand these people.
units.name: VARYA

units.text: Don’t tease her, Peter, you see that she’s quite unhappy without that.
units.name: LUBOV

units.text: She takes too much on herself, she keeps on interfering in other people’s business. The whole summer she’s given no peace to me or to Anya, she’s afraid we’ll have a romance all to ourselves. What has it to do with her? As if I’d ever given her grounds to believe I’d stoop to such vulgarity! We are above love.
units.name: TROFIMOV
